attempts.summary: Discovered that node1 (VyOS) connects node2 via eth1 (192.168.50.0/24) and node3 via eth2 (192.168.60.0/24), with a shared eth0 management network. Assigned static point-to-point addressing on node2/node3 eth1 interfaces plus static routes, confirmed VyOS ip_forward was already enabled, and applied a VyOS QoS rate-control policy (tbf, 1Mbit) on node1's eth2 egress only — the interface facing node3 — so traffic sourced from node2 toward node3 is shaped to 1 Mbit/s while node3→node2 remains on the default unrestricted fq_codel qdisc on eth1. Verified with iperf3: node2→node3 ~0.9-1.05 Mbit/s (down from ~17.8 Gbit/s baseline), node3→node2 ~1.06-1.25 Gbit/s unrestricted. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all three nodes (node2, then node3, then node1), each verified via changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id and confirmed post-restart recovery of interface addressing, routes, VyOS QoS shaper persistence (tc qdisc showed tbf 1Mbit on eth2 survived reboot), and re-verified asymmetric throughput end-to-end after node1's restart.
